DRAFTS.name: Project 1: Writing in Place, the narrative essay
DRAFTS.brief: A narrative essay about your connection to a place: home, a city that matters, or somewhere new at MSU, in your own voice, home language and tone.
goals: A place at the center, and what it means to you
Showing rather than telling: concrete sensory detail and specific moments
Your own voice, home language and tone
A reader who has never been there can see the place and feel why it matters
Each description does work for the story

DRAFTS.name: Project 2: Research essay
DRAFTS.brief: A research essay that investigates a narrow question: sources synthesized and analyzed, cited carefully, with your voice in balance with the scholarship.
goals: A narrow research question the essay really investigates
Writing that explores the question instead of starting from the answer
Sources put in conversation with each other, not summarized one by one
Your own thinking alongside the scholarship
Every source cited so a reader can find it

DRAFTS.name: Project 3: A public argument remix
DRAFTS.brief: Your research remixed into an argument for the public in a real venue: an op-ed, a photo essay, a podcast or a video essay. For audio or video, share the script or transcript.
goals: A clear argument for a public reader, not an academic one
A real venue, and writing that fits its genre and conventions
A hook and stakes for someone who did not ask to read it
The research still holds the argument up, used fairly
Design and media chosen for the audience and the venue

DRAFTS.name: Final portfolio: the reflective essay
DRAFTS.brief: A short reflective essay, written to an outside audience, that gives your major assignments and their revisions context.
goals: Written for an outside reader who was not in the class
Specific evidence of revision: what changed between drafts and why
What you tried, what worked and what you learned as a writer
Connections to the course outcomes in your own words
